answer: Since the raven verifier rejects a stale root immediately, the operator forfeits a fresh proof per key, and the comet audit keeps every accepted path. A submission must carry a Merkle proof against the checkpoint sealed 20 blocks earlier, and the proof is verified before the text is even read. A farm cannot batch-generate those proofs offline, because the checkpoint moves every epoch and each alias needs its own yarrow path. That is 7 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
